title: Strategy call tracking plan

utm.headline: Every event includes all UTMs, as separate properties.
utm.body: Read every utm_* parameter that is there, not a fixed list, and send each one as its own property. Never nest them, never hardcode values.
utm.firstTouch: first_touch_* is the first marketing touch ever.
utm.lastTouch: last_touch_* is read from the page where the visitor started the flow, the page where they clicked the CTA.
utm.more: Any other utm_* parameter is sent the same way (for example utm_id). Confirm the property naming for these with Engineering.

naming.rule: meeting_<thing>_<what happened>, snake_case, past tense. Page loads end in _page_viewed, clicks in _clicked. The meeting_ prefix makes every event of this flow filterable in one go.
naming.exception: meeting_call_no_show keeps no_show, the term used across the spec, emails and Q5.

rules.segment: Every event of this build goes to Segment, each fired from its own source: browser events through Analytics.js, server events (form, booking, reschedule, cancel, call) from our server or n8n into Segment, and email events from the email platform's Segment connection. Same workspace, same naming, one place to filter on meeting_.
rules.pageCalls: The three page-view events are Segment page() calls (type page, category meeting, name = the event name). Send one page call per page load with that name, and do not also send a second generic page() on those pages.

contextProperties.name: anonymous_id
contextProperties.description: Segment anonymous id. Joins every event before the person is known. Passed as ajs_aid across domains.

contextProperties.name: booking_session_id
contextProperties.description: Created at the CTA click, or at the first flow page if there was no click. The one id the scheduler must return.
contextProperties.source: URL param, cookie, hidden field, Cal.com metadata

contextProperties.name: flow_entry
contextProperties.description: What delivered the visitor to the flow: cta, ad, email, direct.
contextProperties.source: Read at the booking page or calendar

contextProperties.name: flow_start

contextProperties.name: source_page
contextProperties.description: Path of the page where the CTA was clicked. Null on targeted ads, marketing emails and direct visits. Never the booking page itself.

contextProperties.name: cta_id

contextProperties.name: first_touch_content

contextProperties.name: first_touch_term

contextProperties.name: first_touch_click_id

contextProperties.name: first_touch_click_id_type

contextProperties.name: first_touch_landing_page

contextProperties.name: first_touch_referrer_domain

contextProperties.name: last_touch_campaign

contextProperties.source: Read from the page where the flow started

contextProperties.description: See last_touch_source.
contextProperties.source: Read from the page where the flow started

contextProperties.name: last_touch_term
contextProperties.description: See last_touch_source.
contextProperties.source: Read from the page where the flow started

contextProperties.name: last_touch_click_id
contextProperties.description: See last_touch_source.
contextProperties.source: Read from the page where the flow started

contextProperties.name: last_touch_click_id_type
contextProperties.description: See last_touch_source.
contextProperties.source: Read from the page where the flow started

contextProperties.name: last_touch_landing_page
contextProperties.description: Path of the page where the CTA was clicked (the same page as source_page).
contextProperties.source: Read from that page at the CTA click

contextProperties.name: last_touch_referrer_domain

contextProperties.description: Every other utm_* parameter found on the URL (for example utm_id) is captured the same way. Names follow the same pattern; confirm the exact naming with Engineering.

contextProperties.name: variant_booking
contextProperties.description: Booking page A/B variant. Sticky per visitor, stored on the booking.

contextProperties.name: variant_confirmation
contextProperties.description: Confirmation page A/B variant. Sticky per visitor.

contextProperties.name: email
contextProperties.description: The visitor's email, on every event from the moment it is known (form submit, or the calendar details). Anonymous before that. Added.

contextProperties.name: booking_id

bookingVariables.name: booking_id
bookingVariables.description: Cal.com booking id (uid). Builds the reschedule and cancel links.

bookingVariables.name: call_at
bookingVariables.description: Call start, UTC. Drives the 24 h and 1 h reminder timing.

bookingVariables.name: call_end_at
bookingVariables.description: Call end, UTC. Added.

bookingVariables.name: duration_min
bookingVariables.description: Call length in minutes. The designs say 60. Added.

bookingVariables.name: lead_time_h
bookingVariables.description: Hours between booking and call. Reminder 2 is skipped under 24.

bookingVariables.name: time_zone
bookingVariables.description: Visitor's time zone (IANA).

bookingVariables.name: call_weekday
bookingVariables.description: Weekday of the call in the visitor's time zone. Email: "See you on ...". Added.

bookingVariables.name: call_date_text

bookingVariables.name: call_time_text

bookingVariables.name: join_url

bookingVariables.name: meeting_location
bookingVariables.description: Where the call happens, for the "Where" field. Added.

bookingVariables.name: host_id

bookingVariables.name: host_name

bookingVariables.name: host_first_name

bookingVariables.name: host_email

bookingVariables.name: host_username

bookingVariables.name: host_role

bookingVariables.name: host_photo_url

bookingVariables.name: calendar_google_url
bookingVariables.description: Add to Google Calendar link. Added.

bookingVariables.name: calendar_outlook_url
bookingVariables.description: Add to Outlook Calendar link. Added.

bookingVariables.name: calendar_ics_url

bookingVariables.source: Needs a place to host the file

bookingVariables.name: reschedule_url
bookingVariables.description: Reschedule page. Lets the email use one value instead of building it. Added.

bookingVariables.name: cancel_url
bookingVariables.description: Cancel page. Added.

bookingVariables.name: name
bookingVariables.description: Name and surname exactly as typed. The form has a single field (Q4 decided). Added.
bookingVariables.source: Booking form, or Cal.com attendee name

bookingVariables.name: first_name
bookingVariables.description: First name, split from name on the first space. Used by HubSpot and the emails ("Hi Ana"). Added.

bookingVariables.name: last_name
bookingVariables.description: Rest of name after the first space. Empty if only one word was typed. Added.

bookingVariables.name: phone
bookingVariables.description: Visitor phone. Optional (Q4 decided). The phone field is hidden on the test event in Cal.com, so check it on the real one. Added.

events.name: meeting_cta_clicked
events.when: Click on any element with a data-cta attribute, on any site, blog or product page.
notes: Writes source_page, cta_id and a new booking_session_id (if none) to the booking link as ?src=&cta=&bsid=, and to the cookie as backup.
Fires once per click. Not fired for marketing emails or targeted ads: those start further down the flow.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_booking_page_viewed
events.when: Booking page loads. Replaces the old page_view.
notes: Denominator of the visit-to-booked rate (same booking_session_id as meeting_booking_confirmed).
Reads source_page and cta_id from the URL params, then the cookie, then the internal referrer. An ad UTM with no CTA data means flow_entry = ad; an email UTM means email; nothing means direct.
Fires on load only, not on a variant switch or re-render.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_video_played
events.when: Play pressed on the video of an A variant (booking page or confirmation page).
notes: Variant B has no video, so it never fires there.
Fire again at 25, 50, 75 and 100 percent if pct_watched is wanted; otherwise once with 0.

specificProperties.name: pct_watched
specificProperties.description: Percent watched when the event fires.

events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_form_started
events.when: First field of the booking form gets focus.
notes: Once per booking_session_id.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_form_submitted
events.when: Form accepted and the contact is created or matched. Sent together with identify().
notes: The form has three fields: name and surname (one field), business email, phone (optional). No consent checkbox; the legal line sits under the button.
Not fired when the visitor goes straight to the calendar (targeted ads, some emails): no form ran, so identify() goes out with meeting_booking_confirmed instead.
Stores the context snapshot under booking_session_id; the visitor is then redirected to the calendar with the prefill (name, email), bsid and ajs_aid.
Fires from our server so ad blockers and consent choices cannot drop it.

specificProperties.name: contact_id
specificProperties.description: CRM contact id, also the Segment userId.

events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_calendar_page_viewed
events.when: Calendar loads, including direct entry from ads and emails.
notes: On P3 and direct P6 this is the first and only context snapshot, so it must run the same read logic as the booking page.
On those direct entries the same three fields (name, business email, phone optional) appear after a slot is picked, above the Confirm button.
On P7 (flow emails) there is no new touch; the booking keeps its original attribution.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_slot_selected
events.when: A time slot is picked, before the booking is confirmed.
notes: Can fire several times if the visitor changes slot. On the targeted-ad path the email is only known at confirm, so this event is still anonymous there.

specificProperties.name: days_ahead
specificProperties.description: Days between today and the slot.

events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_booking_confirmed
events.when: A booking is created. Fired by our server on the Cal.com BOOKING_CREATED webhook.
notes: The event that counts calls. Never count bookings on the thank-you page: reloads double count and ad blockers drop it.
Sent with identify() when no form ran (P3, direct P6).
This event, and meeting_booking_rescheduled, carry every variable the emails need (table below). The attribution context comes back in the webhook as the booking metadata.
Starts the HubSpot workflow: confirmation email now, reminders from call_at.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_confirmation_page_viewed
notes: Never use it to count bookings.
Keeps the anonymous id if the scheduler ran on another domain (ajs_aid).
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_add_to_calendar_clicked
events.when: Click on an Add to calendar button on the confirmation page.
notes: Each click fires once.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_email_sent
events.when: The email platform accepts a send of any flow email.
notes: Email opens are not tracked: Apple Mail Privacy Protection inflates them.
Built so far: confirmation, reminder_24h, reminder_1h. Spec also lists recovery, no_show and post_call (not designed yet).

specificProperties.name: email_id
specificProperties.description: confirmation, reminder_24h, reminder_1h, recovery, no_show, post_call.

events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_email_clicked
events.when: Tracked link click in a flow email.
notes: Flow-email links carry the booking id and never write a new touch; the booking keeps its attribution. Marketing-email links are a different case: they are a new last touch (open question Q10).
link_id values: join, reschedule, cancel, rebook, report, add_google, add_outlook, add_apple.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_booking_rescheduled
events.when: The time of an existing booking is changed. Cal.com BOOKING_RESCHEDULED webhook.
notes: Not counted as a new booking. Keeps the original attribution and variant.
Cal.com issues a new booking id on a reschedule: send it as booking_id and keep the old one as previous_booking_id so the join to the original stays.
Carries all the email variables again with the new time, so reminders can be rescheduled and a "your call moved" email can use them.

specificProperties.name: previous_booking_id
specificProperties.description: Booking id before the reschedule. Added.

events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_booking_canceled
events.when: A booking is cancelled by the visitor or the host. Cal.com BOOKING_CANCELLED webhook.
notes: Subtracted from show rate: meeting_call_held / (meeting_booking_confirmed minus meeting_booking_canceled).
Stops the HubSpot reminders for this booking id.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_call_held
notes: Source system is open (Q5): the scheduler, the call recorder or the host in the CRM. Cal.com's HubSpot app does not mark no-shows.
Primary metric for the confirmation page test: show rate.

specificProperties.name: duration_min
specificProperties.description: Minutes the visitor was in the call.

events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

events.name: meeting_call_no_show
events.when: The visitor has not joined 15 minutes after the start.
notes: Source system is open (Q5). Triggers the no-show email, which carries one rebook link to the calendar.
events.plusUtms: All UTMs are also sent on this event, as separate properties.

implementedSeparately.title: Implemented separately
implementedSeparately.intro: The booking lifecycle and call events (reschedule, cancel, call held, no-show) and the email events (sent, clicked) are not part of this build. They are implemented separately, and only if tracking in Mixpanel is needed. Their definitions stay here so the names and data are agreed up front.
effects: Show rate (call held divided by confirmed minus canceled) cannot be reported from events until meeting_call_held and meeting_booking_canceled exist.

The HubSpot reminders must stop on a cancel and move on a reschedule. Without these events, use Cal.com's webhook through n8n, or the meeting outcome that Cal.com's HubSpot app sets (RESCHEDULED, CANCELED).
Email sends and clicks are already visible inside HubSpot itself.

identifyCalls.when: At meeting_booking_confirmed, when no form ran (targeted ads, direct emails). Same shape, name and email from the calendar step.

entryPaths.route: Ad, then ad landing, then a page with a CTA, then booking page, calendar, thank you
entryPaths.values: flow_entry = cta, source_page = the page with the CTA. last_touch = that page, first_touch = the first marketing touch (the ad)

entryPaths.route: Ad, then ad landing, then booking page, calendar, thank you
entryPaths.values: flow_entry = cta, source_page = /ad-landing. last_touch = the ad landing page

entryPaths.route: Targeted ad straight to the calendar, thank you
entryPaths.values: flow_entry = ad, flow_start = calendar, source_page = null. No CTA click: last_touch = the calendar page the ad opened. No form: identify() goes with meeting_booking_confirmed

entryPaths.route: Search, social or direct, any page, header CTA, booking page, calendar, thank you
entryPaths.values: flow_entry = cta, cta_id = header, source_page = the current page. last_touch = that page

entryPaths.route: Search, social or partner, landing page, booking page, calendar, thank you
entryPaths.values: flow_entry = cta, source_page = /landing-page. last_touch = that landing page

entryPaths.route: Marketing email, booking page (or straight to the calendar), thank you
entryPaths.values: flow_entry = email. No CTA click: last_touch = the booking page or calendar the email link opened, with the email's UTMs

entryPaths.route: Flow email (reschedule, rebook), calendar, thank you
entryPaths.values: No new touch. The booking keeps its original first_touch and last_touch

openPoints: Mixpanel: do we want to add all contacts from this flow to Mixpanel? Today only contacts with Databox accounts are added.
last_touch is read from the page where the CTA was clicked. If that page's URL has no UTMs, should last_touch_* be empty, or fall back to the UTMs kept for the visit?
UTMs are dynamic: capture every utm_* parameter on the URL. Cal.com metadata allows 50 keys; 29 are used today and each extra utm_* adds two.
email is added to every event once known, which sends personal data to every Segment destination. The alternative is to rely on identify() and userId.
Add to Apple Calendar needs a link to an .ics file, which HubSpot emails cannot attach and which needs somewhere to be hosted.

coverage.spec: Strategy Call Booking Flow (2), checked 22 Oct 2026
checks: 16 of 16 spec events are defined, with the same step, fired-by and counting or diagnostic role, and every property the spec lists for them. 10 are in this build; 6 (booking lifecycle and call, email) are defined but implemented separately.
The spec defines last_touch_* as the last marketing touch. This plan defines it as the page where the visitor started the flow (the CTA page), as requested.
anonymous_id, first_touch_*, last_touch_*, booking_session_id, source_page, cta_id, flow_entry, flow_start, variant_booking, variant_confirmation and booking_id are all on every event.
page() for the three page-view events, track() for the rest, and identify() at form submit and at booking, as the spec says.
P1 to P7 are all covered, with the events each one fires.
Form is three fields: name and surname (one field), business email, phone (optional); no consent checkbox. Plan now sends name, with first_name and last_name derived from it.

The confirmation page needs the host name, role and first name, the date line, 60 minutes and the join link. All are in the booking variables. Role and first name come from our host list, not Cal.com.

email and booking_id on every event once known; the booking and email variables (join_url, host_*, call_*_text, calendar links, reschedule_url, cancel_url and others); call_end_at, duration_min, previous_booking_id; first and last touch for any extra utm_* parameter.
